One type covering both cannot be correct for either." **That is false, and it was the record's central premise.** audit.ex:276/295-297 is the INTERNAL return of Letflow.Audit.list_entries/1. lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex:203-204 consumes it, passes has_more to the private next_cursor/2, and then page_body/2 (:308-320) hand-builds %{"items", "next_cursor", "count"} as an explicit INV-2 allowlist. has_more never crosses the HTTP boundary. result.summary: Revision 3. BLOCKER-3 is real, was reproduced by this step rather than inherited, and is closed. Revision 2's diagnosis -- T7 banned a WORD when INV-A is about a FIELD -- was right but its enumeration of code forms was incomplete: it listed three and ES6 shorthand is a fourth, and the commoner one. The tell the gate identified is exact: the renamed destructure { has_more: hasMore } was caught only incidentally, because it contains a colon, while plain { ..., has_more } was not. T7's regex now carries five alternatives, one per way TypeScript can write the field: property access, colon key or type member, string-literal key, ES6 shorthand including destructuring and the multi-line literal form, and a const/let/var binding of that name. Alternatives 4 and 5 are both present deliberately -- 5 catches the defect at its declaration when the literal is built out of sight, 4 catches a shorthand whose binding came from a destructure or a parameter. Re-measured from scratch, not inherited. First a 42-form battery, 27 must-match and 15 must-not: 0 missed, 0 false positives. The must-match set covers eight shorthand and declaration forms revision 2 would have let through; the must-not set covers all four real prose comments, section 4's two required docblock sentences, backtick-then-colon AND backtick-then-comma AND backtick-then-brace prose -- the three shapes alternatives 2 and 4 come closest to mis-firing on -- and six TimelineFeed hasMore forms including the shorthand and const spellings only the new alternatives could have caught. Then the discriminating A/B, with the exact defect written back into promotions.ts's .then in shorthand form: arm A, revision 2's regex, tsc -b --force exit 0 AND source-scan 0 violations -- both gates pass it, BLOCKER-3 reproduced; arm B, the five-alternative regex, nothing else changed, source-scan FAILS with 'Source scan found 1 violation(s): has-more-wire-field @ web/src/api/promotions.ts:262' while tsc -b --force still exits 0. tsc being identical across both arms is the point: it is the same non-freshness-checked return position section 8 item 3 recorded, so T7 is the only gate that can move there, and only once corrected. Clean tree under the new regex: tsc exit 0, guards 4 files / 52 tests all passed with source-scan at zero, npm run test 125 files / 890 tests passed. Section 7's overclaim is withdrawn -- the T7 row now says the guard catches every realistic code spelling and is a backstop, not a proof of impossibility, and section 7.1 has a new 'what this guard does and does not prove' paragraph naming the two forms that would still evade it (a parameter binding typed only by inference, a key assembled by string concatenation) and explaining why widening further would re-create BLOCKER-1. The durable fix for the class stays ISS-0813. T8's offender fixture now exercises all five alternatives, so the shorthand alternative is mechanically pinned rather than only documented; the bystander gains const hasMore and { items, hasMore } so it also stresses alternatives 4 and 5. Section 6.3 and T9 are rewritten around the asymmetry the gate measured: T-0765-SURFACE at :229 goes red on its own, but T-0765-NO-ADMIN-PREFIX at :252-259 stays GREEN and silently under-covers, because it.each iterates a hand-maintained array rather than Object.keys, so an implementer who fixes only the failing assertion drops the new function from ISS-0765's prefix coverage with no signal anywhere. The design now says that plainly and states the row is added deliberately, not in response to a red test. Section 8 item 8's count is corrected to 14 occurrences across 7 files, with the reason the earlier 8 was wrong spelled out -- it mixed web/src with web/tests, and obs04.timeline.e2e.spec.ts is outside source-scan's src/** glob. surfaceRows cited at :252-259 throughout. Everything else the gate verified is carried forward unchanged.

result.how_the_section_4_t7_contradiction_was_r: By narrowing the guard to the field, not the word. T7 exists to serve INV-A, which is about a field being declared or accessed -- not about the nine characters appearing anywhere in the tree. Revision 1 conflated the two, which is what made section 4's required docblock illegal and what made identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63 a false positive. The narrowed regex matches only the three ways TypeScript can express the field: a property access (\.has_more\b), an object-literal or type-member key (\bhas_more\s*\??\s*: -- which also covers the optional form has_more?: boolean), and a string-literal key (["']has_more["']). Prose is structurally safe because comments name the field inside backticks, and a closing backtick is neither whitespace nor a colon. The alternatives the gate listed were both rejected and the trade-offs are recorded in the design: exempting web/src/types/api.ts would gut the guard at the single most important file it protects, and rewording section 4 to avoid the literal token would cost section 4 its stated purpose, which is to name the field explicitly so nobody re-files ISS-0816 for a sixth time. The accepted cost of narrowing -- a bare has_more in prose outside backticks and not followed by a colon is no longer caught -- is stated in section 7.1 rather than left for a reader to discover.

corrected_t7_spec.name: has-more-wire-field
alternatives: 2. \bhas_more\s*\??\s*: -- object-literal key, type member, optional member, renamed destructure { has_more: hasMore }

4. \bhas_more\s*[,}] -- ES6 SHORTHAND, the BLOCKER-3 gap: { items, next_cursor, has_more }, { has_more }, const { has_more } = page, function f({ has_more }), and the multi-line literal where the closing brace is on a later line, since \s spans newlines and source-scan tests whole-file content before locating a line
5. \b(?:const|let|var)\s+has_more\b -- a local binding of that name, which is how shorthand gets something to be shorthand for
corrected_t7_spec.why_4_and_5_both: 5 catches the defect at its declaration even when the literal is assembled somewhere the other four cannot see; 4 catches a shorthand whose binding came from a destructure or a function parameter rather than a declaration. Either alone leaves a hole.
corrected_t7_spec.exemption_set_rationale: Exactly two files, unchanged across all three revisions, both for the same reason: each still writes the CODE form has_more: false. Both are ISS-0821 fixtures and the inline comment says both exemptions are deleted when ISS-0821 lands. web/src/types/api.ts and web/src/api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts need NO exemption -- clearing those two without exempting them is what closed BLOCKER-1 and BLOCKER-2 together, and the added alternatives 4 and 5 do not disturb it, because prose names the field inside backticks and a closing backtick is neither whitespace, colon, comma nor brace.
corrected_t7_spec.limits_stated_not_hidden: Not a proof of impossibility. A binding obtained from a function parameter typed only by inference, or a key assembled by string concatenation, would evade it. Neither is how this defect has ever been written, here or in the five prior sightings, and widening far enough to cover them would start matching prose again -- which is what caused BLOCKER-1. T7 is a backstop; the durable fix for the class is ISS-0813's mechanical coupling of web/src/types/api.ts to the routers' real response bodies.

fixtures.offender: web/tests/guards/fixtures/offender/has-more-wire-field.txt -- must exercise ALL FIVE alternatives so each is mechanically pinned: an object-literal key (has_more: false), a property access (page.has_more), a const declaration, an ES6 shorthand literal ({ items, next_cursor, has_more }), and a renamed destructure (const { has_more: renamed } = body). Alternative 4 is what BLOCKER-3 was about; without a fixture form for it, it would be the only alternative no test protects and the next edit could silently drop it again.
